articles.title: Where are the spec sliders?
articles.summary: Click a zone card in the left column to open the ZONE POPOUT PANEL.
articles.what: Three sliders (-127 to +127) that push the whole zone's spec map: R = metal, G = roughness (low = mirror), B = clearcoat. Pushes the METAL channel (-127 to +127). More metal = the body colour flashes harder.
when: You asked: Where are the spec sliders?
how: Click a zone card in the left column to open the ZONE POPOUT PANEL.
Open the BASE section and scroll to "Spec Sliders": R Metal, G Rough, B Coat.
Strength of the whole spec is "Spec Strength" higher up in BASE.
pitfalls: B Coat is inverted in iRacing terms - the number moves clearcoat strength, see the tooltip. Spec only changes in the spec map and in iRacing; the flat colour preview may look unchanged.

faq.q: Where do I find Spec Sliders (R Metal, G Rough, B Coat)?
faq.a: ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE > Spec Sliders. Three sliders (-127 to +127) that push the whole zone's spec map: R = metal, G = roughness (low = mirror), B = clearcoat.

faq.q: Where do I find R Metal?
faq.a: ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE > Spec Sliders. Pushes the METAL channel (-127 to +127). More metal = the body colour flashes harder.
Make the zone shinier / more metallic / matte without changing the finish: "make the spec shinier only".

mistakes.cause: The shine was judged in the colour view, which cannot show it
mistakes.fix: Open the R METAL, G ROUGH and B COAT views in the preview.

protips: Look at the three spec views, not only the colour view; most surprises hide in the spec.

deep.heading: What you need first
deep.body: You need a zone first. This works in Pro mode.

deep.heading: The controls involved
deep.body: Spec Sliders (R Metal, G Rough, B Coat) (ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE > Spec Sliders): Three sliders (-127 to +127) that push the whole zone's spec map: R = metal, G = roughness (low = mirror), B = clearcoat; R Metal (ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE > Spec Sliders): Pushes the METAL channel (-127 to +127). More metal = the body colour flashes harder; G Rough (ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE > Spec Sliders): Pushes ROUGHNESS (-127 to +127). Lower = sharper mirror flashes, higher = soft satin glow; B Coat (ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE > Spec Sliders): Pushes CLEARCOAT (-127 to +127). 16 is max gloss: minus = glossier (stops at 16), plus = duller.

deep.heading: When this comes up
deep.body: Make the zone shinier / more metallic / matte without changing the finish: "make the spec shinier only". Metal looks too weak or too much. Too shiny or too dull.

articles.title: Why is my zone not showing / doing anything?
articles.summary: Does it have an area (colour, layer, or box) AND a finish?
articles.what: Quick checks for "Why is my zone not showing / doing anything". The controls involved are Zone order (drag handle and priority), COLOR (section), Base Material (finish picker button).
when: You asked: Why is my zone not showing / doing anything?
how: Does it have an area (colour, layer, or box) AND a finish? The panel warns "No color or region set yet".
Is a zone ABOVE it claiming the same pixels? Drag it higher.
Is the colour tolerance too tight? Raise it.
Is the zone muted (eye icon off) or limited to a hidden layer?
Is the preview stale? Press the Refresh button or F5.
pitfalls: A zone with no colour, layer or box set does nothing ("No color or region set yet" warning).
Foundation (f_*) finishes change only the spec when colour = Use source paint; bases like chrome / candy repaint the zone.
aliases: why is my zone not showing doing anything

faq.q: Where do I find Zone order (drag handle and priority)?
faq.a: Left column > zone cards (drag the handle). Top zone wins where two zones select the same pixels.

ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > COLOR. Decides WHICH PIXELS of the paint this zone owns: by clicked colour, by PSD layer, or as catch-all (Remaining).
"Why is my zone not showing?" - another zone above it already claims those pixels.

faq.q: What do I need before I start?

mistakes.cause: Another zone higher in the list claims the same pixels
mistakes.fix: Drag your zone higher, or mute the others to test.

mistakes.symptom: The preview looks stale or wrong
mistakes.cause: It was not refreshed after a change
mistakes.fix: Press F5 over the preview, then diagnose.

protips: Mute every other zone to test one zone quickly.

deep.heading: What you need first
deep.body: You need a zone first. This works in Pro mode.

deep.heading: The controls involved
deep.body: Zone order (drag handle and priority) (left column > zone cards (drag the handle)): Top zone wins where two zones select the same pixels; COLOR (section) (ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > COLOR): Decides WHICH PIXELS of the paint this zone owns: by clicked colour, by PSD layer, or as catch-all (Remaining); Base Material (finish picker button) (ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE): Opens the finish picker popup: bases (gloss, matte, satin, chrome, candy, pearl, metallic ...) and special looks. Shows the current finish name.

deep.heading: When this comes up
deep.body: "Why is my zone not showing?" - another zone above it already claims those pixels. You say "only the red parts" or "only the numbers". Choose or change the finish of this zone.

combos.why: The full troubleshooting article: every cause, the fix steps and how to confirm.
RESTRICT TO LAYERS (checkboxes per PSD layer): Tick a layer (Car Paint, Sponsors, Numbers, Tape ...) and the zone only covers pixels that exist on that layer.
PICK COLOR FROM CAR: Arms an eyedropper: click a colour on the car and this zone grabs every pixel of that colour. Each further click ADDS another colour.
Finish picker search box: Search finishes in the base picker by name, idea or #tag.

articles.title: How do I change the order or priority of zones?
articles.summary: In the left ZONES column drag a zone card by its handle (the three-line icon).
articles.what: Top zone wins where two zones select the same pixels.
when: You asked: How do I change the order or priority of zones?
how: In the left ZONES column drag a zone card by its handle (the three-line icon).
Top = highest priority; where two zones select the same pixels the higher one wins.
A catch-all "Remaining" zone belongs at the bottom.
